module_title: Input/Output Devices - Display Metrics, Speed Measurements, and I/O Ports
introduction: Tailored for IT Specialist Officers (Bank SO), SSC CGL Tier-2, and advanced technical papers, this module analyzes monitor display terminology, the specific metrics used to measure printer speed and quality, and legacy vs. modern hardware connection ports.

core_concepts.title: Monitor Display Terminology
core_concepts.description:
- Pixel (Picture Element): The smallest physical point or dot on a display screen.
- Resolution: The total number of pixels on the screen (Horizontal × Vertical). Higher resolution means sharper images.
- Dot Pitch: The diagonal distance between two pixels of the same color. A lower dot pitch results in a crisper, sharper image.

core_concepts.title: Display Panel Technologies
core_concepts.description:
- CRT (Cathode Ray Tube): Bulky, legacy monitors using vacuum tubes.
- LCD (Liquid Crystal Display): Uses liquid crystals sandwiched between polarized glass.
- LED (Light Emitting Diode): Actually an LCD that uses LEDs for backlighting instead of fluorescent lamps.
- OLED (Organic LED): The most advanced; pixels produce their own light, requiring no backlight and offering infinite contrast.

core_concepts.title: Printer Quality and Speed Metrics
core_concepts.description:
- Quality/Resolution: Measured in DPI (Dots Per Inch).
- Speed: Measured in three evolutionary stages:
  1. CPS (Characters Per Second) - Used for Dot Matrix/Daisy Wheel.
  2. LPM (Lines Per Minute) - Used for Line Printers (Drum/Chain printers).
  3. PPM (Pages Per Minute) - Used for modern Laser and Inkjet printers.

core_concepts.title: Computer I/O Ports
core_concepts.description:
- Serial Port: Transmits data one bit at a time (used for legacy mice/modems).
- Parallel Port: Transmits multiple bits simultaneously (traditionally a 25-pin port used exclusively for legacy printers).
- USB (Universal Serial Bus): The modern standard supporting 'Plug and Play'.
- VGA/HDMI: Video Graphic Array (analog video) and High-Definition Multimedia Interface (digital video AND audio).

important_entities.name: Refresh Rate
important_entities.significance: Measured in Hertz (Hz). It represents how many times per second the monitor redraws or updates the image on the screen. A low refresh rate causes screen 'flickering' and eye strain.

important_entities.name: Digitizer (Graphic Tablet)
important_entities.significance: An input device that converts analog information (like drawing with a stylus on a flat pad) into digital format. Widely used in CAD and professional digital art.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A major technical trap! Candidates often assume that 'higher' is always better in technology. However, Dot Pitch is the *distance* between pixels. Therefore, a LOWER dot pitch means the pixels are closer together, yielding a much BETTER image quality.
Do not confuse printer metrics. DPI (Dots Per Inch) strictly measures print QUALITY (resolution). PPM (Pages Per Minute) strictly measures print SPEED.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Printer speed evolved logically: first, they printed one Character at a time (CPS), then a whole Line at a time (LPM), and now a full Page at a time (PPM).

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-2 analytical exams, you will be tested on port functionality. Remember that the legacy 'Parallel Port' (LPT) was synonymous with connecting printers, while 'HDMI' is unique because it carries both high-definition video AND audio simultaneously.
